pull.title: KAFKA-19035: Honor configured GlobalKTable deserialization handlers in TopologyTestDriver
pull.body:
`TopologyTestDriver` always used `LogAndContinueExceptionHandler` for global-store input, ignoring configured fail and custom handlers. Use `StreamsConfig.deserializationExceptionHandler()` to match `GlobalStreamThread`. Malformed global input now fails with the default handler.

Preserve inherited `Properties` settings so inherited handlers work correctly. Other inherited settings also become effective, including `state.dir` and `application.id`, which determine application state cleaned on close. Includes regression tests and an upgrade note.

Related to [KAFKA-19035](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-19035). This PR covers GlobalKTable deserialization-handler selection in TopologyTestDriver and the associated configuration preservation; DLQ delivery remains outside its scope.

commit.message:
KAFKA-19035: Honor configured GlobalKTable deserialization handlers in TopologyTestDriver

`TopologyTestDriver` always used `LogAndContinueExceptionHandler` for global-store input, so malformed `GlobalKTable` records were skipped even when the configured handler should fail, and custom handlers were never invoked. Use `StreamsConfig.deserializationExceptionHandler()` to match `GlobalStreamThread`, with regression coverage and an upgrade note explaining how to retain continue-on-error behavior.

Related to KAFKA-19035. This is a partial fix limited to GlobalKTable/global-store deserialization-handler selection in the test driver. It does not implement DLQ delivery or complete KAFKA-19035; that ticket should remain open. Global-thread DLQ support remains tracked separately in KAFKA-20280.

@@ -67,6 +67,8 @@ Since 2.6.0 release, Kafka Streams depends on a RocksDB version that requires Ma
 
 ## Streams API changes in 4.5.0
 
+`TopologyTestDriver` now honors the configured deserialization exception handler for `GlobalKTable` records. With the default handler, malformed records throw `StreamsException`; configure `LogAndContinueExceptionHandler` to keep skipping them. Inherited `Properties` defaults now apply to all settings, including `state.dir` and `application.id`, which determine the application state cleaned on close.
+
 Processors returning the same `StoreBuilder` instance from `ConnectedStoreProvider#stores()` are now grouped into one subtopology ([KAFKA-20464](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20464)). For affected applications, task IDs change and state is restored from the changelog on first startup after upgrading. Linking processors to a store by name is unaffected.
 
 Upgraded RocksDB dependency to version 10.10.1(from 10.1.3). RocksDB deleted `max_write_buffer_number_to_maintain` from its `ColumnFamilyOptions` in version 10.5.0. To preserve compatibility, Kafka Streams' `Options#setMaxWriteBufferNumberToMaintain` and `Options#maxWriteBufferNumberToMaintain` are now deprecated no-ops: the setter has no effect, and the getter always returns `0` regardless of what was previously configured. This change is primarily relevant to users implementing custom RocksDB configurations via `rocksdb.config.setter`. Users relying on `max_write_buffer_number_to_maintain` should remove that configuration, since it no longer has any effect. Consult the [RocksDB changelog](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/HISTORY.md) between 10.1.3 and 10.10.1 for other changes.
